subtitle: Musical Pitch Correction
tagline: Real-time monophonic pitch correction that keeps a vocal in your key and scale, and lets ambiguous notes follow the direction of the melody.

body.lead: TB Tune is a real-time pitch corrector for a single voice. It keeps the performance inside the key and scale you choose, with a more musical sense of direction than simply snapping to the nearest note.

body.p: When a sung note lands between two scale notes, `AUTO MUSICAL` considers the previous stable note and the direction of the melody before it chooses the target, so rising lines can keep rising and falling lines can keep falling. Each decision stays fixed for the whole note. `FORMANT` changes the vocal character without moving the corrected note.

ul: Key wheel for the 12 keys, and 16 scales from Major to Diminished
`AUTO MUSICAL` sets how often ambiguous notes follow the melodic direction
`FORMANT` from −6 to +6 semitones, independent of the corrected pitch
Pitch-status display with the input note, target note, cents offset, and voicing

steps: Target note from KEY, SCALE, and AUTO MUSICAL

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Tune 2.1.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 1.0.4 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Tune on a solo vocal or another monophonic, pitched track.
Click the song's key on the `KEY` wheel. The default is C.
Choose a scale group (MODES, MINOR, PENTA, or SYM), then the scale. The default is Major (Ionian).
Play the track and watch the display: INPUT shows the detected note, TARGET the note it is corrected to.
Raise `AUTO MUSICAL` if the correction picks the wrong neighbour on fast or sliding lines.
Adjust `FORMANT` only if you want a darker or brighter character.

TARGET shows the note being corrected to and its cents offset; INPUT shows the detected note.
Vocal character shift. Double-click to type a value in semitones.

note.text: TB Tune follows one voice at a time. Chords, doubled vocals, and heavy reverb confuse pitch detection, so use it on a dry, solo track.

body.p: Use the preset controls to step through presets, or open the list to choose Init or one of your user presets. Save stores the current settings as a .tbautotunepreset file. The name shows CUSTOM after you change a setting.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Natural correction
recipes.use: A pop or rock lead vocal that should still sound human.
steps: Check that the target notes match the melody before raising Auto Musical.

recipes.title: Fast, melismatic lines
recipes.use: Runs and slides where notes pass between scale steps.
steps: Watch for AUTO MUSICAL CHOICE on the display while the run plays.

recipes.title: Minor-key song
recipes.use: A song in a minor key with raised leading tones.
settings: Harmonic Minor or Melodic Minor Ascending
steps: Natural Minor has no raised seventh, so a raised seventh is corrected to a neighbouring note. Choose Harmonic Minor if the melody uses it.

recipes.title: Character shift
recipes.use: A darker or brighter voice for a double or a character.
steps: Small values change character; large values sound processed.

rows: Correct notes are pulled to wrong pitches.
KEY or SCALE does not match the song. Check both.
The display shows WAITING FOR VOICED INPUT.
The input is silent, unpitched, or too noisy. Use a dry, solo vocal.
Vibrato and expressive slides are flattened.
Lower AUTO MUSICAL, or check whether the scale has too few notes.
The voice sounds unnatural after correction.
Set FORMANT to 0 st and use a scale that fits the melody.
It does not work on a choir or chords.
TB Tune is monophonic. Use it on single-voice tracks.

Redesigned the editor with a brighter key-and-scale workflow, a dedicated pitch-status panel, and higher-resolution controls. The pitch engine, parameter IDs, and saved-state compatibility are unchanged.
Rebuilt the interface around direct key-note and scale selection with a dedicated pitch-status panel, expanded the scale choices, and made the Auto Musical and Formant controls easier to read.
